t: This is Albert Bridge, carrying the road over the Thames from Chelsea on the north bank to Battersea on the south. Rowland Mason Ordish designed and built it in 1873, but it proved structurally unsound. Between 1884 and 1887 Sir Joseph Bazalgette added elements of a suspension bridge, and in 1973 the Greater London Council added two concrete piers. So it's an unusual hybrid of three design styles, and it's Grade II* listed. It is named after Prince Albert, Queen Victoria's husband.
